sources.citation: Kempf, Viktoria & Tamara Prischnegg. 2020. A sketch of Akum (Southern Jukunoid). Afrika und Übersee 93: 299-326. DOI 10.15460/auue.2020.93.1.215 (neighbouring language; already held by the project under akum1238)
sources.note: About Akum, not Bezen; mentions Bezen only comparatively (tonally dominated TAM system, vowel lengthening, noun prefixes). No stress statement for either language.

sources.citation: Essegbey, James. 2019. Review of: Viktoria Kempf, 2017, Verbal Serialisation in Bezen (Southern Jukunoid). Linguistique et Langues Africaines 5. DOI 10.4000/lla.506
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Reports that Kempf 2017 ch. 2 begins with 'the phonology and morphology of verbs. Topics discussed include syllable structure, vowel harmony, and tone'.

sources.citation: Kempf, Viktoria. 2018. Kuteb verbal extensions vs. Bezen verbal serialisation: a comparison. Linguistique et Langues Africaines 4: 31-53. DOI 10.4000/lla.9938
sources.note: Nothing on stress. States Bezen verbal roots are CV, VC or CVC; valency change and adverb derivation marked by tonal pattern shifts (HM>MH, ML>HM, HL); adhortative/obligative marked by tonal change only. Cites Tabah (forthcoming) 'Elision and Contraction in Bezen Phonology' (PhD, Buea) and Fogwe-Chibaka & Akumbu 2012 'Unreleased final consonants in Bezen'.

sources.citation: Kempf, Viktoria. 2014 [2013]. Remnants of a noun class system in Bezen (Southern-Jukunoid). Afrikanistik-Aegyptologie-Online (Tagungsband Afrikanistentag 2012). DOI 10.18716/ojs/aaeo/2014_3411
sources.note: Nothing on stress; noun-class morphology paper. Uses H/M/L tone marking throughout (prefix tone 'prescribed by the tonal value of the root'); root shapes CVC/CV/VC; vowel allophony footnote.

sources.citation: DoBeS project 'Documentation of the Bezen language (Cameroon)' (Roland Kießling & Viktoria Kempf, Univ. Hamburg; VW Foundation 2011-2015), project web description, page 'Language', dobes.mpi.nl, published 2013-09-23 / modified 2013-11-14
sources.note: Nothing on stress/accent. Phonology paragraph gives consonant subsystems, six vowels /i e ɨ a o u/, 'Three contrastive level tones distinguish grammatical as well as lexical meanings' (hú 'die' / hū 'gather' / hù 'fall'), syllable types V, VC, CV, CVC.

sources.citation: Akumbu, Pius & Elizabeth Brye. 2005. A rapid appraisal language survey of Akum and Beezen. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2005-019.
sources.note: The source Glottolog/earlier scan named; survey only, listed for completeness (unlikely to treat stress).
